reviewer.evidence:

Every message identical to the English source (the only case that can hide leftover English prose) was individually classified as a formatting template, keyboard key name, internationally standardized abbreviation/unit, Jupyter notebook convention, or a named cross-language cognate/loanword, and each carries an entry-specific rationale rather than a boilerplate sentence; none were found to be untranslated prose. Full-catalog key coverage, key order, placeholder names and this locale's CLDR plural categories are separately and unconditionally enforced by check-translations.mjs for every shipped catalog, independent of this ledger. AI-assisted; no human or native-speaker review is claimed, and no broader message-by-message linguistic register re-audit beyond the English-identical set is claimed. Updated 2026-09-27 for statusIncomplete ("Incomplete") and toolCallBlockHeaderIncomplete ("Did not finish using {name}"). An AI-assisted review, separate from the contributor that drafted them, checked both values in this catalog for the meaning of a tool call that ended without a result (an interrupted stream or a cancelled run), UI register, consistency with this catalog's neighbouring tool-call status and block-header wording, and exact single {name} preservation; both were approved without correction and no English-identical allowlist entry was required. No human or native-speaker review is claimed. Updated 2026-09-28: an independent AI-assisted review checked all 69 added messages for meaning, UI register, terminology and placeholders, and corrected the catalog before this snapshot. The research-source count was checked against the pinned CLDR categories, including locale-specific decimal and non-singular forms. The complete 1,384-key snapshot was checked for key coverage, value kinds, placeholders and exact-English message paths; only individually justified new cognates, loanwords and technical names were retained. This increment does not claim a new linguistic review of all older messages, human review or native-speaker certification.
